subject: Stormbridge commitment runway: token lanes and QoS fallback plan
messages:
From: Ariane Morin <ariane@stormbridge.ai>

Cc: Stormbridge Sales <sales@stormbridge.ai>, Luca Bianchi <luca.b@stormbridge.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood demo follow-up + workload details

Jordan — thanks again for the demo this morning. Our CTO asked for a short write-up on expected throughput and what commitment tiers would look like given our workload. A couple specifics:

- Typical request profile: single-turn instruction -> 60-120 tokens generated (median 80).
- Peak concurrency: 180 concurrent requests during business hours (PST) with spikes up to ~420 for marketing bursts.
- Quality target: 95% of requests under 300ms p95 for short prompts; p99 target is softer (we can accept up to 600ms if needed).

Can you provide a tokens/sec estimate for a dedicated pool run (model we saw: open-llama-XXL-16k, FP16 / 8-bit quant) and suggested headroom for a 24/7 commitment vs burst-capacity? I attached our short questionnaire.

Also: procurement will need wording on burst guarantees and fallback model behavior for degraded capacity.

Thanks — Ariane

--

Ariane — really helpful context, thanks. I took a first-pass at the numbers and attached a small spreadsheet (stormbridge-token-estimates.xlsx) with the assumptions. High-level callouts below; Ben (cc) and Irene are on standby for deeper sizing.

Summary (first-pass):
- Baseline tokens/sec (sustained) per H100-equivalent GPU: ~1,100 tokens/sec for short-gen (80 tokens) with FP16 and moderate batching.
- A100-class is ~650-800 tokens/sec for the same profile (depends on optimizations).
- With a 24/7 committed slab and automated KV caching we estimate needing ~12 H100-equivalent GPUs to cover average load (including 20% cold-cache penalty).
- For spikes (420 concurrent) and p95 300ms target, add ~40% headroom -> ~17 GPUs total to meet SLO without burst credits.
- Recommended commitment tiers: 12 GPUs (reserve), + 6-10 flexible burst GPUs (on-demand pool) with policy-based fallback to smaller quantized model if load exceeds burst.

I'll let Ben/Irene chime in with more concrete latency mapping and tensor-level notes. For procurement language on burst guarantees, we can propose a soft-burst SLA (best-effort) and subscription credits for guaranteed burst windows.

Jordan

Subject: Internal: Stormbridge slab mapping and latency-to-tps math

Folks — I ran a quick slab-level model and tradeoffs. Putting the core numbers here so we can finalize the send to Stormbridge tomorrow. I've attached a one-pager PDF with the slab mapping. Key technical assumptions and results: 

Assumptions:
- Model: open-llama-XXL-16k variant; sequence length distribution centered at 180 tokens total (prompt+gen) but generation portion median 80 tokens.
- Hardware: H100 perf baseline; we normalize other SKUs to H100-equivalent tokens/sec.
- Execution: FP16 runtime with 4-bit activation quant enabled under non-critical paths; KV cache hit reduces work by ~35% on repeat prompts.
- Batching: continuous batching with target batch window 8-12ms for low-latency apps.

Numbers (rounded):
- Sustained tokens/sec per H100-equivalent (median): 1,100 tps
- P95 tokens/sec (accounting for jitter, cold-cache): 760 tps
- P99 stress tokens/sec (peak small-batch inefficiency): 420 tps

SLO mapping (Stormbridge targets):
- p95 latency <= 300ms: requires ~1,100 tps sustained capacity per GPU; for 180-concurrency baseline (median) we need 15 GPUs to sustain without relying on bursts.
- Peak spike (420 concurrency) to achieve p95 300ms: need ~22 GPUs (no caching). With hot KV caching and warm pools we can reduce to ~17 GPUs.

Headroom guidance:
- Conservative commitment (recommended for predictable cost): commit 14 GPUs, paired with 6 flexible burst GPUs managed by Redwood Dedicated. That gives ~30% headroom for unmodeled tail events and planned growth.
- Aggressive optimized option: commit 10 GPUs + 12 burst credits and an auto-fallback to a quantized model for non-critical traffic; saves on committed spend but requires careful fallbacks and eval gating.

Operational notes / fallbacks:
- Fallback model runway: we can route >90% of non-critical/long tail requests to a 4-bit quantized variant with expected tokens/sec uplift of ~30% per GPU but ~10-12% quality delta on some prompts.
- Cold-start mitigation: keep a small warm pool (2 GPUs) across regions during US business hours to maintain p99 latency behavior.
- Monitoring hooks: expose route-level p95/p99 and token-velocity dashboards; set automatic rollback to quantized fallback when p99 latency breaches threshold for 5+ consecutive minutes.

Questions for Jordan/Ariane before I formalize the MA(Plan):
1) Do they want a firm committed-count pricing (monthly) or a hybrid commit+burst credit model?
2) Any regulatory constraints that force on-prem or VPC-only options (affects placement of warm pool)?

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Stormbridge: proposed mutual action plan and next steps

Ariane / Luca — circling back with a concise mutual action plan based on Ben's slab math. Attachments: stormbridge-token-estimates.xlsx, stormbridge-slab-mapping.pdf.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) 2-week technical validation: Redwood provides a 14-GPU committed test slab (H100-equivalent) for 2 weeks with full telemetry. Objective: validate p95/p99 behavior and KV cache hit rates on your real traffic.
2) Performance review checkpoint: at day 10 Ben/Irene will run a p95/p99 comparison and recommend +6 GPUs of burst capacity if needed.
3) Contracting: if validation meets p95 300ms target for >=95% of sampled traffic, Stormbridge signs a 12-month commitment for 14 GPUs; we include 120 burst credits (equivalent to ~6 GPUs' monthly capacity) for predictable short-term spikes.
4) Fallback policy: automatic routing to quantized model when sustained p99 breaches threshold; quality gate will be set by Stormbridge (we'll include rollout knobs in Redwood Console).

Ask: Can procurement review the soft-burst language below and greenlight it for legal to draft?
"Redwood will provide best-effort burst capacity during defined spike windows; guaranteed burst capacity may be procured as an addon. Redwood will surface burst health and failures in the Console."
If that looks OK I'll have legal and finance produce an LOI with preliminary pricing tied to the 14-GPU commit + burst credits model. If Stormbridge prefers a smaller commit with more burst credits instead, we can present the alternate price schedule.

Ariane — happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow for procurement + engineering if you want to finalize the contract language.

Thanks,
Jordan
